subject: bobbit worm
title: This Worm Can Be 10 Feet Long and You Never See It Coming

scenes.text: A worm this long hides under the seafloor and you never see it.
The bobbit worm can grow up to three metres, about ten feet, but it buries almost all of itself.
Only five antennae stick out of the sand. Fish swim right past them.
It senses the movement, and then the sand explodes.
Its jaws snap shut, so hard the fish is often sliced in half.
Then it drags the pieces down into the burrow. The ocean's longest ambush is a worm you walked right over.

description:
The bobbit worm can grow up to three metres long, yet hides almost entirely under the sand with only its antennae showing.
When a fish passes, it lunges and snaps its jaws shut, often slicing prey in half, then drags it into its burrow.
Would you dive on a reef knowing this lives there? Comment below.
first_comment: Bobbit worms have been found in aquariums, hidden in live rock, and have shocked owners by cutting fish in half. Would you keep one?
